request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- **Who made the change:** the signed-in name is only in the browser's URL, so the person and claim forms now send it with each save in an `X-User` header (`api/http.ts`, `features/people/form.slot.tsx`, `features/claims/list.slot.tsx`). The name is URI-encoded because a header can't carry non-Latin characters, and the server decodes it (`AuditUser.java`).
- **Writing the line:** each of the four save endpoints has a new `audit` step that runs after the save and before the response: `AuditPersonAdded`, `AuditPersonEdited`, `AuditClaimAdded` and `AuditClaimEdited`. Claim lines are built in `ClaimAudit`, which writes the amount with two decimals and the date as yyyy-mm-dd.
- **Refused changes write nothing:** every refusal happens before the audit step, so a refused change never reaches it. Person and claim edits now also write to the database before the audit line (`saveAndFlush`). Without that, a duplicate name caught only when the transaction commits would leave an audit line for a change that never happened. New people and claims are already written to the database before their line.

**One trap I hit:** `@RequestHeader(value = "X-User")` quietly came back empty with no error, so the first run logged `by=` with no name. OfficeFloor only reads the `name =` form of that annotation, and switching to `@RequestHeader(name = "X-User", required = false)` fixed it. I checked this with a direct request to the server before re-running the tests.

**Worth knowing:** the name goes into the line exactly as typed, so a name containing a space will appear with that space in `by=`. This only applies to the four events in the request; changing the sheet's today date still writes nothing.
